picks.style: sanskrit recitation, tanpura drone, deep male voice, slow, reverent, sparse
picks.why: The sages approaching Yama in his hermitage, and water made pure by wind, sun, stars and the two twilights.

picks.style: dark ascetic chant, damaru and low drone, rough male voice, grave, hypnotic, slow
picks.why: For each single sin a penance is known; when all sins converge, only the skull-bowl of the Kāpālika remains.

picks.style: hellenistic hymn, kithara and double aulos, radiant female chorus, building, luminous, ceremonial
picks.why: The swans circling seven times, the birth, and the whole island turning gold — lake, olive, river and all.

picks.style: invocation hymn, solo lyre, clear male voice, sea-wind atmosphere, measured, reverent
picks.why: The opening address to Delos, windswept and barren, haunt of gulls, fixed fast in the deep.

picks.style: island dance hymn, aulos, frame drum and foot-stamping, mixed chorus, circling, joyous
picks.why: No sailor passes without furling sail to dance round the altar and bite the holy olive; ends on a hail.

picks.style: greek elegy, single lyre, intimate male voice, quiet, unhurried, mournful
picks.why: Heraclitus is ash, but his nightingales live and Hades will never lay a hand on them.

picks.style: graveyard dialogue song, plucked lyre and low drone, two voices trading lines, dry, dark, spare
picks.why: Charidas answering from the grave: the ways up are a lie, and Pluto is a tale.

picks.style: sardonic epigram song, lyre and hand drum, wry male voice, clipped, brisk
picks.why: I hate the cyclic poem and drink from no public fountain — the poet's manifesto in six lines.

picks.style: georgian parlour song, fortepiano and flute, light tenor, tripping, mock-defiant
picks.why: Go, idle Boy! I quit thy pow'r — a dismissal of Cupid with a ready-made refrain of freedom.

picks.style: romantic art song, piano and cello, warm baritone, unhurried, sea-lit
picks.why: Standing on the shore at sunset, crimson on the flood and gold on the curling surf, when the song reaches him.

picks.style: anti-war ballad, solo fiddle and muted drum, grave male voice, slow, bitter
picks.why: Conquest distilling a general poison from the laurel leaf, and the line that victory is defeat.

picks.style: ancient chorus, kithara and aulos, layered voices with soprano lead, shimmering, building, awed
picks.why: Theseus among the Nereids, Amphitrite's purple cloak and rose wreath, and his rise from the sea unwetted.

picks.style: heroic chorus, lyre and frame drum, firm male voice against chorus, defiant, steady
picks.why: Theseus refusing Minos: he would not want to see the light of Dawn if a girl were forced.

picks.style: narrative ode, aulos and lyre, bright male voice, portrait-like, animated, moderate
picks.why: The stranger described head to foot — Lemnian fire flashing from his eyes — closing on the paths of song.

picks.style: tragic aria, solo cello and low drone, strong female voice, slow, indignant, mounting
picks.why: Medea's complaint, ending on the line that she would rather fight three times than give birth once.

picks.style: comic women's chorus, aulos and tambourine, sharp female voices, quick, sardonic
picks.why: The women's counter-attack on Euripides — every broken dish now proof of a lover from Corinth.

picks.style: encomium in the high style, lyre, declamatory male voice, grand, ironic, measured
picks.why: The least-bad passage: praise pitched above the gods, closing on the weeping dame, a match for goddesses.

picks.style: oracular chant, low drone and single bell, ambiguous whispered-then-declaimed male voice, slow, uneasy
picks.why: The two-faced prophecies — Pyrrhus and the Romans, the duke who shall depose Henry — riddles built to be sung.
